children: TL;DR
Base network activity reached roughly 7.5 million transactions over a single day in the validated September 22 data.
The count includes all recorded transactions, including low-value and automated activity.
High transaction count is a usage metric, not proof of equivalent economic value.
Base has pushed daily transaction activity to roughly 7.5 million, adding another scale milestone for Coinbase’s Ethereum Layer 2 ecosystem.
The number is eye-catching, but the more interesting question is what it says about the type of activity happening on the network.
Cheap Transactions Change What Users Put Onchain
Layer 2 networks make it economical to record interactions that would be too expensive to justify on Ethereum mainnet.
That can include social actions, wallet automation, small trades, game events and application-level transactions that may carry very little individual dollar value.
As a result, a transaction record can reflect genuine adoption while also including a large amount of automated or micro-transaction activity.
That distinction is important when comparing Base with networks where each transaction is more expensive and therefore tends to represent a different mix of use cases.
Base Keeps Expanding Beyond Simple DeFi
The network’s growth has increasingly come from consumer-facing apps, smart wallets and social or commerce products alongside conventional DeFi.
That broader application mix can generate far more transactions than a chain built mainly around high-value financial settlement.
For Coinbase, Base also creates a distribution layer that sits underneath its wider product ecosystem.
Users can move from exchange accounts into onchain applications without leaving the company’s broader orbit.
A 7.5 million transaction day does not tell us how many unique humans were active or how much economic value moved.
It does show that Base is handling activity at a scale where throughput and infrastructure efficiency matter.
The next question is whether that usage persists when incentives or individual applications cool down.
Daily transaction records are easy to celebrate. Sustained user retention is the harder metric.

Base also benefits from a distribution advantage that most Layer 2 networks do not have: a direct connection to one of the largest consumer crypto platforms. That does not guarantee that exchange users become onchain users, but it lowers the friction when Coinbase chooses to surface Base-native experiences. The harder challenge is making activity sticky once users arrive. A chain can generate millions of daily interactions around one popular application and still see usage fall sharply later. The 7.5 million figure is therefore impressive, but retention and economic value per user will tell the more durable story.
This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Base Activity Climbs To 7.5 Million Transactions In A Day
